title: Column orchestration and personalized layout presets for large grids
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a first-class system for users to reorder columns at-scale, save personalized column layouts (presets), and gracefully handle reordering interactions when many columns are virtualized/offscreen. Deliver accessible keyboard flows, mobile fallbacks, and a small API surface so Product teams can expose layout presets in their UIs.
acceptance_criteria: Users can reorder columns by drag-and-drop across visible and offscreen columns without losing position when virtualization recycles cells
Keyboard-only users can move a focused column left/right and receive clear aria announcements and focus stability
Users can save the current column configuration as a named preset and switch between presets (persisted per-user in cloud)
Presets survive model rollouts and minor schema changes (column hidden/renamed) with sensible fallbacks
Compact fallback layout collapses non-critical columns into a summary column on narrow viewports; toggleable via an affordance
Unit and E2E tests cover drag across virtualization boundary, preset save/load, keyboard reordering, and mobile fallback
Design tokens used for drag handles, focus rings, and reorder ghost are consistent with DS tokens and high-contrast mode
design_notes: Problem: existing reordering breaks when virtualization unmounts columns mid-drag. We need a drag model that targets column indices rather than DOM nodes and prefetches adjacent column metadata while dragging.
Proposal: implement an index-based drag anchor + a lightweight placeholder layer rendered outside the virtualized scroller so ghost/preview remains stable.
Accessibility: add a keyboard reorder mode (Cmd/Ctrl+M to enter), then use arrow keys + Enter to move. Announce moves via aria-live with messages like 'Column "Customer" moved to position 3'.

Presets: client saves presets to the user profile via a small PUT /user/layouts endpoint (PM/ENG to define shape). Include a local fallback (localStorage) when cloud sync unavailable and a conflict indicator if server preset diverges.
Compact fallback: instead of hiding columns automatically, show a compact summary column with a density-aware token that reduces padding and font-size to DS-compact values. Users can expand inline.
Telemetry: capture metrics for reorder frequency, preset save rate, keyboard vs mouse reorder, and failures when save returns 4xx/5xx
Tradeoffs considered: server-sided canonical order vs purely client-managed presets. Chosen: client-first with optional server persist to avoid latency on every reorder.
Performance: minimize reflows by avoiding heavy DOM updates during drag; use transform-based ghost layer and update column order only on drop.
Edge cases: column renamed or removed in downstream updates -> map saved preset keys to current column IDs and mark mismatches in UI for user repair
